checklist: websocat --version is 4.0.0-alpha3; the installed THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md covers the linked crates (tokio, mio with homescoop's patches, rustls, ring, webpki-roots), the wasix-org Rust standard library and wasix-sysroot

kernel loopback as cone (users enforce), server `websocat -s <port> mirror:`: text lines echo in order; -b binary 1 MiB and 16 MiB round trips are byte-equal (the slow-peer case, 64 KiB loopback buffers: needs mio/0001); five concurrent clients all echo (repeated accept); a closed port is rc 14 'Connection refused'

frames, raw over tcp: the upgrade answers 101 with the RFC 6455 Sec-WebSocket-Accept; a ping gets a pong with the same payload; a close with code 4000 is echoed as 4000; a text frame then close 1000 echo back in order
no exit or tailnet: a hostname fails with rc 21 (os error 44) and an outer address with rc 14 'Network unreachable', quickly (no hang)

outer ws:// and wss:// through a kernel uplink (test/uplink.mjs, slicc-kernel's Node entry, users enforce, the uplink dials host-side echo servers; echo.test resolves through the uplink): two text messages and a ~3.9 MB binary message echo byte-equal over ws://; wss:// with -k echoes (the TLS handshake and framing, rustls); wss:// without -k refuses the throwaway CA (chain verification against the embedded webpki roots is on; verification of a real chain is slicc-bios's end-to-end); a refused uplink port is rc 14 (needs mio/0003), a name the uplink doesn't know rc 21; the servers see Host and SNI echo.test
